scope: Real container generation migration on the disposable fresh fixture: one SIGKILL at the named durable checkpoint, the resulting startup refusal, the repeated-migration refusal, exactly one reconciliation, and the recreated container with its resource tier and per device block IO limits on the same pgdata volume. No retained placement resource was touched.
evidence: the fixture database is pinned before after-rules
the retired container is running before after-rules
the retired pgdata volume is the fixture volume
the migration process died at the exact after-rules checkpoint
the crash left the migration record in place
the checkpoint the crash follows is durable
ordinary startup refuses while the record is present
the refused startup changed neither the pin nor the record
a repeated migration refuses while the record is present
the interrupted migration reconciles once
a second reconciliation refuses
the pin names the recreated container with one new generation
the migration record is gone after completion
the recreated container carries its resource tier
the recreated container carries its per device block IO limits
the recreated container mounts the same pgdata volume
the recreated container publishes no host port
the new registry holds one retired token of the new generation
the evidence binds the retired generation and its last observed digest
the evidence states the rule comparison instead of implying byte equality
the retired pin bytes are archived, never rewritten
startup is admitted again after reconciliation and the recreated database is running
the recreated database kept every environment database
the recreated database kept its guard rows
